questions.question: According to recent UNFPA estimates, 68 per cent of India’s population is between _____ years of age in 2022.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 and 64**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA),** as of** 2022, 68% of India's population **falls within the **age group of 15 to 64 years**, representing the working-age population of the country.
 
• The UNFPA's 2023 State of World Population Report further indicates that 25% of India's population is between 0 and 14 years old, 18% falls between 10 and 19 years old, and 7% are over the age of 65.
 
• **India** currently holds the title of the most populous country globally.
 
• Estimates suggest that by mid-2023, India's population is projected to reach approximately 1.4286 billion (142.86 crores), surpassing China's population of around 1.4257 billion (142.57 crores).
 
• This large population can be attributed to "population momentum," a phenomenon stemming from previous demographic trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA),** formerly known as the** United Nations Fund for Population Activities,** is a UN agency focused on improving reproductive and maternal health globally.
 
• Its efforts include developing national healthcare strategies, expanding access to contraception, and leading campaigns against practices like child marriage and gender-based violence.
 
• The UNFPA operates in over 144 countries across four regions: Arab States and Europe, Asia and the Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Africa.
 
• It is the world's largest multilateral source of funding for population and reproductive health programs.

questions.question: Which Indian musician’s autobiography is titled ‘Raga Mala’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Raga Mala"** is the autobiography of renowned Indian classical musician **Ravi Shankar, released in 1997.**
 
• It is a limited edition publication by **Genesis Publications, **featuring a hand-bound design with an initial print run of 2,000 signed and numbered copies.
 
• Notably, **George Harrison **contributed the foreword and served as Shankar's editor for the book.
 
• Containing a curated selection of photographs and documents sourced from Shankar's personal archives, "Raga Mala" provides readers with an intimate glimpse into the musician's life and career.
 
• The idea for the autobiography arose in 1994, when Harrison persuaded Shankar to embark on the project as a means to commemorate his 75th birthday.
 
• Following extensive research, interviews, and writing, the book was published to widespread acclaim and success.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ravi Shankar **was a celebrated Indian sitarist and composer, renowned for his virtuosity and mastery of North Indian classical music. Throughout the latter half of the 20th century, he gained global recognition as the foremost authority on this genre, exerting a profound influence on musicians both in India and around the world.
 
• **Vishwa Mohan Bhatt,** professionally known as V. M. Bhatt, is a distinguished Hindustani classical music instrumentalist renowned for his expertise in playing the Mohan veena.
 
• **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, born on March 9, 1951, is an eminent Indian tabla player, composer, percussionist, music producer, and film actor. He is the eldest son of the legendary tabla maestro Alla Rakha, and he himself has achieved immense acclaim for his contributions to the world of music.

questions.question: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple, which is dedicated to Shiva and was constructed in 999 by the Chandela dynasty, is an example of which of the following styles of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagara style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kandariya Mahadeva temple **exemplifies **Nagara-style architecture,** also known as the idol Nagara style, and is renowned as one of** India's finest temples.**
 
• It stands as a prominent example of central Indian architecture and follows the** Panchayatana style**, akin to Kalinga architecture in its arrangement.
 
• Commissioned by** King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty** in 999 CE, the temple is dedicated to the deity Shiva.
 
• Situated in the Khajuraho village at an altitude of 925 feet, it enjoys convenient accessibility via road, rail, and air routes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Originating in northern India during the **5th century CE, the Nagara style **is widespread in regions such as **Malwa, Rajputana, and Kalinga, **spanning states like Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal.
 
• The term "Nagara" denotes "city," reflecting the style's association with urban architectural principles.
 
• Nagara temples typically feature a square or rectangular layout, with a central shikhara (tower-like spire).
 
• These spires often assume a pyramidal shape, with the curvature of the Latina less pronounced.
 
• Nagara temples boast a distinct fusion of indigenous elements and influences from Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian architecture,** also known as the Southern Indian temple style, is a distinctive architectural tradition in Hindu temple architecture that evolved in Southern India, reaching its pinnacle by the sixteenth century.
 
• **The Ahom architectural style** is characterized by its amalgamation of diverse cultural, traditional, and religious influences.
 
• **The pagoda structure **is inspired by the stupa, an ancient Indian commemorative monument with a hemispherical, domed shape, which served as the basis for its design.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest text of ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rig Veda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rigveda** stands as the oldest known text of ancient India, penned in** Sanskrit circa 1500 BC.**
 
• As the earliest among the** Vedas, the sacred scriptures of Hinduism,** it comprises 1,028 hymns partitioned into 10 sections known as mandalas.
 
• These hymns venerate Rigvedic deities and are frequently recited during religious rituals.
 
• Notably, the Rigveda holds the distinction of being one of the oldest extant texts in any **Indo-European language.**
 
• Additionally, the Bakhshali manuscript preserves the earliest documented instance of a zero being utilized as a placeholder in India.
 
• Within this manuscript, a dot signifies the origin of the zero symbol currently employed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Mahabhashya**, attributed to Patañjali, serves as a commentary on specific rules of Sanskrit grammar derived from Pāṇini's renowned treatise, the Aṣṭādhyāyī, alongside Kātyāyana's Vārttika-sūtra, which provides an in-depth elaboration on Pāṇini's grammatical principles.
 
• **The Arthashastra** stands as an ancient Indian Sanskrit text focusing on various aspects of statecraft, political science, economic policy, and military strategy, offering comprehensive insights into governance and administration.
 
• **The Manusmriti,** alternatively known as the Mānava-Dharmaśāstra or Laws of Manu, represents one of the prominent legal texts within the corpus of Dharmaśāstras in Hinduism. It addresses diverse aspects of moral and legal principles, delineating guidelines for societal conduct and individual behavior.

questions.question: Which union territory has the highest sex ratio value according to the 2011 census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **2011 census data, Puducherry** boasts the **highest sex ratio **among all union territories, with **1037 females for every 1000 males.**
 
• Following closely behind are** Lakshadweep (946), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (878), Kashmir (883), and Sikkim (889), **which also exhibit relatively high sex ratios.
 
• Conversely, the union territories with the **lowest sex ratios **include **Daman and Diu (618), Dadra and Nagar Haveli (775), and Chandigarh (818).**
 
• The sex ratio serves as a crucial demographic indicator, representing the proportion of females to every 1000 males within a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 2011 Indian census**, also known as the **15th Indian census,** was carried out in two distinct phases: the house listing phase and the population enumeration phase.
 
• Commencing on 1 April 2010, the house listing phase entailed the comprehensive collection of data pertaining to all buildings across the nation.
 
• Additionally, this phase included the gathering of information for the National Population Register (NPR), intended for the issuance of a 12-digit unique identification number to every registered Indian resident by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).
 
• Subsequently, the population enumeration phase took place between 9 and 28 February 2011, during which demographic data of the populace was meticulously recorded.

questions.concept: Awards and Honours, Art and Culture
questions.question: Who among the following musicians was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar,** a sitar player, composer, and founder of the **National Orchestra of India, **received **India's highest civilian honor**, **the Bharat Ratna**, in **1999**.
 
• Throughout the latter half of the 20th century, he attained global recognition as the foremost exponent of North Indian classical music.
 
• Born in Benares (now Varanasi) in 1920, Shankar passed away in San Diego, California, in 2012.
 
• He garnered numerous prestigious musical accolades, including a **Polar Music Prize** and** five Grammy Awards**. Notably, he won Album of the Year for **"The Concert for Bangladesh"** in 1973.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, born on March 9, 1951, is an Indian tabla player, composer, percussionist, music producer, and film actor. Recognized for his contributions, he received the Padma Shri in 1988, the Padma Bhushan in 2002, and the Padma Vibhushan in 2023 from the Government of India.
 
• **Ram Narayan,** an Indian musician, significantly popularized the sarangi as a solo concert instrument in Hindustani classical music, becoming the first internationally successful sarangi player.
 
• **Ustad Amjad Ali Khan,** renowned for his clear and fast ekhara taans on the sarod, is an Indian classical sarod player. He was honored with the Padma Vibhushan in 2001, the Padma Bhushan in 1991, and the Padma Shree in 1975, among India's highest civilian awards.

questions.question: What is the distance between the two goal posts in a football match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.32 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The distance between the **two goal posts in a football match** is **7.32 m**.
 
• In a **football match**, the goalposts are the vertical structures located at each end of the playing field. These goalposts are used as targets for scoring goals.
 
• The distance between the two goal posts is standardized according to the Laws of the Game, which govern football matches worldwide.
 
• According to the regulations set by the **International Football Association Board (IFAB),** the organization responsible for determining the rules of football, the distance between the two goal posts is** 7.32 meters (8 yards).**
 
• This distance is measured horizontally from the inside edge of one goalpost to the inside edge of the opposite goalpost.
 
• Maintaining a consistent distance between the goal posts ensures fairness and uniformity across football matches, allowing players to accurately aim their shots and facilitating fair play.

questions.question: What is the ratio by mass of carbon and oxygen in carbon dioxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 ∶ 8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The chemical formula of carbon dioxide is CO₂.**

Atomic mass of carbon is **12**.

Atomic mass of oxygen is **16**.

Mass ratio = 1 x 12 : 2 x 16

= 12 : 32

**= 3 : 8**

questions.question: Which of the following is a Rabi crop in Northern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mustard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mustard **is a **Rabi crop **in **Northern India.**
 
• **Mustard** is categorized as a **Rabi crop, **typically sown during the period from** October to November** and harvested **between March and April.**
 
• This oilseed crop flourishes in dry and cool climates, necessitating cooler temperatures for optimal growth.
 
• It is extensively cultivated in India, with yellow varieties predominantly cultivated in regions such as Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Rabi crops,** also referred to as winter crops, are agricultural crops planted during the winter season and harvested in spring.
 
• The term** "Rabi" originates from the Arabic word "rabi,"** signifying the fourth part or spring.
 
• These crops are typically cultivated in dry regions and necessitate regular irrigation for growth.
 
• The Rabi season typically commences in November and extends until March or April.
 
• Farmers sow the seeds at the onset of autumn to coincide with the onset of the Rabi season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice, cotton, and maize** are predominantly considered as **Kharif crops. **

questions.question: Which of the following pair of dances belongs to Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali and Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam** pair of dances **belongs to Kerala**.
 
• Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are classical dance forms originating from Kerala, India.
 
• **Kathakali **is renowned for its **theatrical elements,** including elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, expressive face masks, and ornate ornaments.
 
• **Mohiniyattam **is characterized by its graceful movements, predominantly performed by women.
 
• It is often described as a blend of **Kathakali and Bharatanatyam styles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kathakali **remains popular in India, preserving its traditional practices. With over 500 Attakatha plays, many dating back to before the 20th century, Kathakali has a rich repertoire.
 
• Recent productions have expanded its horizons by incorporating stories from various cultures and mythologies, including those of Miguel de Cervantes, Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, and William Shakespeare.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is celebrated for its elegance, typically performed as solo recitals by female dancers.
 
• The name "Mohiniyattam" derives from "Mohini," the feminine aspect of Lord Vishnu, signifying the "dance of Mohini."
 
• The dance narrates the tale of Mohini, an enchantress avatar of the divine in Vaishnavism.

questions.question: From the given alternatives, identify the dwarf planet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pluto,** a** dwarf planet** situated in the **Kuiper Belt, **orbits the Sun beyond **Neptune's orbit.**
 
• Discovered in **1930 by Clyde Tombaugh, Pluto **was initially regarded as the** ninth planet.**
 
• However, in** 2006, the International Astronomical Union **reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.
 
• Despite being the largest known trans-Neptunian object by volume, Pluto is less massive than Eris.
 
• It holds the distinction of being the best-known dwarf planet, boasting the largest size and the second-largest mass among its peers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pluto **possesses at least five moons, namely **Charon, Nix, Styx, Kerberos, and Hydra.**
 
• Charon, the largest moon, dwarfs Pluto, measuring more than half its size.
 
• With an orbit characterized by significant elongation and inclination compared to the planets, Pluto's distance from the Sun fluctuates between 29.7 AU at its nearest point and 49.5 AU at its farthest.
 
• In 2015, NASA's New Horizons spacecraft conducted a flyby of Pluto and its moons, unveiling a diverse landscape featuring mountains, valleys, plains, craters, and potentially glaciers.

questions.question: The Jhelum River rises from which of the following sources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spring at Verinag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Jhelum River **originates from the **Verinag spring **situated in the **Kashmir Valley**, nestled at the base of the **Pir Panjal range in Anantnag.**
 
• It traverses through **Srinagar and Wular Lake** before exiting into Pakistan via a narrow gorge.
 
• As the westernmost of the five rivers in the** Punjab region, **the Jhelum spans a length of 725 kilometers.
 
• Functioning as a tributary of the Chenab River, the Jhelum flows across the Indian-administered territory of Jammu and Kashmir, subsequently entering Pakistani-administered Kashmir, and eventually reaching the Pakistani province of Punjab.
 
• Its course meanders northwestward from the northern slopes of the Pir Panjal Range, traversing the scenic Vale of Kashmir until it reaches Wular Lake in Srinagar, where its flow is regulated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Verinag Spring, **situated in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India, is renowned for its deep blue water, sourced from the base of a mountain spur.
 
• The Brahmaputra River originates from the **Chemayungdung glacier** within the Kailash range near Lake Mansarovar.
 
• **Lake Mansarovar, **located in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, holds the distinction of being the highest freshwater lake globally, with an elevation of 14,950 meters.
 
• **Lake Rakshastal,** alternatively known as Rakshas Tal, is a saltwater lake located in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

questions.question: Peeling, cutting or crushing onion tissue releases which enzyme that makes our eyes water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allinases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **an onion's tissue is peeled, cut, or crushed,** it releases enzymes known as **allinases**. These enzymes facilitate the **conversion of certain molecules** into sulfenic acids.
 
• These sulfenic acids then undergo spontaneous rearrangement to form **syn-propanethial-S-oxide**, the chemical compound responsible for triggering tears. This process involves the conversion of the onion's sulfoxides into sulfenic acid by the allinase enzyme.
 
• The resulting sulfenic acid subsequently rearranges itself into syn-propanethial-S-oxide, which irritates the lachrymal glands in the eyes, leading to the release of tears.
 
• Moreover, the allinase enzyme also plays a role in the creation of another volatile compound called **lachrymatory factor (LF)**.
 
• This LF compound, generated by the action of allinase, diffuses into the air and interacts with the nerves of the cornea, inducing an involuntary tearing response.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Xylanases **constitute a category of enzymes responsible for the degradation of xylan, a complex polysaccharide abundant in plant cell walls.
 
• **Pectinases **are enzymes specialized in breaking down pectin, another polysaccharide component prevalent in the cell walls of plants.

questions.question: Which of the following women personalities has the honour of being a ‘Double Medalist’ at the Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P V Sindhu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PV Sindhu**, the sole** Indian female athlete **to secure c**onsecutive Olympic medals,** clinched a** silver in 2016 and a bronze in 2020**.
 
• She stands as the first Indian woman and the fourth overall in women's singles badminton to achieve this feat.
 
• Sindhu boasts an impressive track record with victories in various prestigious tournaments including the** Olympics and on the BWF circuit,** highlighted by her gold medal at the 2019 World Championships.
 
• Recognized for her outstanding contributions to sports, she has been honored with the **Arjuna Award, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Padma Shri, and Padma Bhushan**, among other prestigious accolades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• During the 2016 Summer Olympics, **Sakshi Malik** secured the bronze medal in the 58 kg category, marking her as the inaugural Indian female wrestler to achieve Olympic glory.
 
• In the 2012 Olympic Games held in London, England, **Saina Nehwal**, the Indian badminton player, claimed the bronze medal in women's singles.
 
• Back in 2000, **Karnam Malleswari **scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to clinch an Olympic medal.

questions.question: Ganesh Chaturthi is observed in ________ month of Hindu calendar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhadrapada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Hinduism, Ganesh Chaturthi** is a** ten-day celebration **commemorating the** birth of the elephant-headed god Ganesha**, who is known as the knowledge and prosperity god.
 
• It starts on the fourth day, or chathurthi, of **Bhadrapada**, the **sixth month in the Hindu calendar**, which runs from **August to September.**
 
• Ganesha idols are set up on elevated platforms in houses or in ornately decorated outside tents before the beginning of the celebration.
 
• The 16 ways of offering tribute, or shhodashopachara, come first in the worship, after which is the pranapratishtha, a rite to bring life to the idols.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bhadrapada** is the sixth month of the Hindu calendar, occurring in August and September, and is one of the four holy months of Chaturmas.
 
• **Kartika,** the eighth month of the Hindu calendar, is also the seventh month in India's national civil calendar, spanning from October 23 to November 21 in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• **Ashadha,** the fourth month of the Hindu calendar, aligns with June or July in the Gregorian calendar, starting from June 22 to July 22.
 
• **Vaishakh, **the second month of the Indian national calendar, corresponds to April or May in the Gregorian calendar.

questions.question: How many Fundamental Duties are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Indian Constitution** enshrines **11 fundamental duties for citizens**, delineated in** Article 51-A.**
 
• Originally, the Constitution solely included fundamental rights without any mention of fundamental duties.
 
• However, in **1976, the 42nd Amendment Act **introduced 10 fundamental duties.
 
• Subsequently, in 2002, the 86th Constitutional Amendment appended an 11th fundamental duty.
 
• These fundamental duties are as follows:

 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and adhere to the noble ideals that guided our national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and foster the spirit of common brotherhood among all citizens, transcending religious, linguistic, regional, or sectional differences; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to demonstrate compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop a scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and renounce violence.
 
• To strive for excellence in all spheres of individual and collective endeavor, ensuring that the nation continuously ascends to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• For parents or guardians, to provide opportunities for the education of their children or wards between the ages of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: There shall be a _______ with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Council of Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There shall be a **Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister** at the head to aid and advise the** President of India**.
 
• **Article 74(1) of the Constitution of India** stipulates that the President of India shall be assisted and advised by a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• The President is mandated to act in accordance with the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers.
 
• However, the President retains the prerogative to request the Council of Ministers to review their advice, yet must ultimately adhere to their counsel following reconsideration.
 
• **The 42nd Amendment of the Constitution of India,** enacted in 1976, explicitly delineated that the President is bound to act in accordance with the advice tendered by the Council of Ministers.
 
• This amendment was ratified on** January 3, 1977,** thus solidifying the principle of executive accountability and the supremacy of the Council of Ministers in guiding the President's actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Council of States,** commonly referred to as the Rajya Sabha, serves as the upper house of the Indian Parliament. As a federal chamber, it holds special powers as outlined in the Constitution.
 
• **An advocate general **of a state holds a senior position within the legal system, providing legal counsel and representation to the state government.
 
• **The Attorney General for India** serves as the principal legal advisor to the Government of India. Appointed by the President of India upon the recommendation of the Union Cabinet in accordance with Article 76(1) of the Constitution, the attorney general holds office at the pleasure of the President.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder and director of the ‘Darpana Academy of Performing Arts’, an institute that focuses on training students in dance, drama, music and puppetry, in the city of Ahmedabad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mrinalini Sarabhai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mrinalini Sarabhai** was the founder and director of the** ‘Darpana Academy of Performing Arts’,** an institute that focuses on training students in dance, drama, music and puppetry, in the city of Ahmedabad.
 
• **Mrinalini Sarabhai and Vikram Sarabhai **founded the **Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in 1949, **situated in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai, distinguished as an Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and educator, pioneered an innovative approach to dance.
 
• Renowned for her pioneering spirit, she became the first woman to master the traditionally male-dominated Kathakali style.
 
• Recognized for her contributions, she was honored with the** Padma Shri in 1965 and the Padma Bhushan in 1992**.
 
• In 2016, she passed away at the age of 97, leaving behind an enduring legacy.
 
• Mallika Sarabhai, daughter of Mrinalini and Vikram Sarabhai, has diligently led the academy for the past three decades, preserving its rich traditions and fostering artistic excellence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amala Shankar **was an eminent Indian dancer, celebrated for her contributions to the world of performing arts.
 
• **Sitara Devi** was a renowned Indian dancer who excelled in the classical Kathak style, in addition to being a skilled singer and actress.
 
• **Padmini Chettur **is a distinguished Indian contemporary dancer, whose artistic journey was shaped under the guidance of the acclaimed dancer-choreographer, Chandralekha.

questions.question: Under _____ a new policy of “paramountcy” was initiated. In this policy the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Hastings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Lord Hastings** a new policy of** “paramountcy” **was initiated. In this policy the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.
 
• **Lord Hastings, **serving as the** Governor-General of India** from **1813 to 1823**, **implemented the policy of paramountcy.**
 
• This policy asserted the supremacy of the** British East India **Company's authority over Indian states, justifying their annexation or the threat thereof.
 
• It granted the Governor-General the power to intervene in the internal affairs of princely states and even supersede their authority when deemed necessary.
 
• This policy remained in effect for 45 years, from 1813 to 1858. During this period, the British solidified their dominance and established themselves as the ultimate authority over Indian territories.
 
• However, they did not formally integrate Princely India into their claim over the Indian subcontinent. Following the uprising of 1857, known as the Indian Rebellion or the First War of Independence, the British initiated the sub-ordinate unity program.
 
• This program aimed to strengthen British control and governance, ultimately lasting until India gained independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Charles Cornwallis**, a British Army officer, Whig politician, and colonial administrator, is renowned for his role as one of the prominent British generals during the American War of Independence.
 
• **Thomas Munro,** a Scottish soldier and British colonial administrator, served as an officer in the East India Company's army and later became the governor of the Madras Presidency.
 
• **Robert Clive, **famously known as Clive of India, was the inaugural British Governor of the Bengal Presidency.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT belong to class Insects?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scorpion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Scorpion **does NOT belong to class Insects.
 
• **Scorpions **are **arachnids characterized **by **their eight legs** and **nocturnal carnivorous habits**.
 
• They **inhabit diverse environments, **ranging from deserts and plains to savannas, forests, rainforests, and even caves.
 
• One unique feature of scorpions among arachnids is their method of reproduction. Unlike most other arachnids, which lay eggs, scorpions give birth to live young.
 
• This reproductive strategy is known as ovoviviparity, where the eggs develop and hatch inside the female's body, and the young are then born live.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Insects,** derived from the Latin term "insectum," are hexapod invertebrates of the** class Insecta**.
 
• They have a chitinous exoskeleton, a three-part body (head, thorax, and abdomen), three pairs of jointed legs, compound eyes, and a pair of antennae.
 
• They are the largest group within the arthropod phylum and the most diverse group of animals, with more than a million described species, representing more than half of all animal species.
 
• Most insects reproduce by laying eggs. The insect nervous system consists of a brain and a ventral nerve cord.

questions.question: Who among the following was the author of the book ‘Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ziauddin Barani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ziauddin Barani **was the author of the book **‘Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi’.**
 
• **The Tarikh-i Firoz Shahi **stands as a remarkable example of **Indo-Persian historiography** from the Sultanate era in India.
 
• Completed in **1357 CE**, it was dedicated to the reigning monarch of the time.
 
• Ziauddin Barani, an Indian Muslim political thinker** during the reigns of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firuz Shah**, was renowned for his authorship of the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi (also known as Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi).
 
• This historical work provides insights into medieval India, spanning from the rule of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq to the initial years of Firuz Shah Tughluq's reign.
 
• Barani's Fatwa-i-Jahandari, while promoting a hierarchy among Muslim communities in the Indian subcontinent, was not strictly based on race or caste.
 
• It drew inspiration from the Sassanid Iran model, which emphasized aristocracy through birth.
 
• This concept, according to some scholars, aligned with the evolving Islamic thought of the time, as evident in the works of contemporaries like Ibn Khaldun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Minhaj-us-Siraj** was a Persian historian born in the Ghurid region during the 13th century. In 1227, he migrated to Ucch and later settled in Delhi.
 
• **Abu Fazl **was an Indian writer, historian, and statesman who held the position of grand vizier in the Mughal Empire from his appointment in 1579 until his passing in 1602.
 
• **Syedna Mohammed Badruddin **served as the 46th Da'i al-Mutlaq of the Dawoodi Bohra community. He succeeded Syedna Tayyeb Zainuddin as the religious leader.

questions.question: The executive power of the Union in India rests with _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As per the Indian Constitution**, the **executive authority of the Union** is vested in the **President,** who may exercise it directly or through subordinate officers.
 
• However, the practical exercise of executive power is primarily conducted by the **Council of Ministers,** under the leadership of the Prime Minister.
 
• The Prime Minister, a member of **either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha**, must meet certain eligibility criteria.
 
• They must be **at least 25 years old if they are a Lok Sabha member, or at least 30 years **old if they are a Rajya Sabha member.
 
• Additionally, they must be a citizen of India and cannot hold any profit-making office under the Indian government.
 
• While there is no term limit for the Prime Minister, they must maintain the confidence of both the President and the Lok Sabha to remain in office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The President of India **is elected by an electoral college composed of elected members from both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of the states.
 
• This election is conducted through the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote method.
 
• To ensure fairness and equity, each vote is given suitable weightage to maintain uniformity among states and parity between the states and the Union.
 
• The President must fulfill certain eligibility criteria, including being a citizen of India, at least 35 years of age, and qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Their term of office spans five years, and they are eligible for re-election. Removal from office follows the procedure outlined in Article 61 of the Constitution.
